answer: Use cipher receipts with a 90-day horizon. A newcomer locks a $150 bond, and each real job ends with the client signing a cipher receipt chained to the last one, so entries cannot be faked later. After 25 receipts over 45 days, three established peers verify the chain and call two clients to check. Pass and the bond returns. Fail once and the bond burns, plus a 60-day wait. Forging 1,000 identities needs $150,000 in bonds and 25,000 genuine client signatures, about 6,250 hours of work. A fake agent is a vertex with no edges: it looks linked until someone tugs and it falls apart.
